reden: Yes. The audit report explicitly flags the same reentrancy in Cred._createCredInternal: createCred writes creds[credIdCounter], then calls buyShareCred before incrementing credIdCounter; the buy path refunds ETH before state updates and there is no nonReentrant guard, enabling reentry into createCred to reuse the same credId and overwrite creator/URL/type/bondingCurve. This is the identical root cause and code path as the described H-06 (reentering createCred via the refund to overwrite the cred before the counter increments). While the report’s impact focuses on integrity/overwriting, the vulnerability description highlights a more severe economic exploit (switching to a more expensive bonding curve to drain ETH). Both exploits stem from the same flaw and would be fixed by the same mitigation (add nonReentrant/CEI or increment before external call). The report also separately notes the refund-before-lock write enabling immediate sell, which the H-06 scenario leverages. Therefore, the audit detected the same vulnerability.
